title: DICS: Data-Informed Centroid Splitting for Decision Tree Classifiers
abstract: arXiv:2608.20258v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Decision tree-based models are widely used in machine learning due to their interpretability and strong empirical performance. However, training decision trees can be computationally expensive, particularly for large and high-dimensional datasets, largely due to the exhaustive search over candidate splits at each node. To improve computational efficiency, we propose Data-Informed Centroid Splitting (DICS), a clustering-based framework that constructs a compact and informative set of candidate splits using data-driven priors. By incorporating class-aware structure, DICS significantly reduces the split search space for classification tasks while preserving predictive performance. We further provide theoretical analysis showing that under the stated assumptions, DICS does not degrade the performance of classification trees compared to exhaustive split search. DICS can be incorporated into classification trees, random forests, and gradient-b

translated_title: DICS：面向决策树分类器的数据知情质心分裂方法
translated_abstract: 基于决策树的模型因其可解释性和强大的实证性能在机器学习中被广泛使用。然而，训练决策树在计算上可能非常昂贵，尤其是在处理大型和高维数据集时，这主要归因于在每个节点上对候选分裂进行穷举搜索。为了提高计算效率，我们提出了数据知情质心分裂（DICS），这是一种基于聚类的框架，利用数据驱动的先验信息构建一个紧凑且信息丰富的候选分裂集。通过融入类感知结构，DICS显著减少了分类任务中的分裂搜索空间，同时保持了预测性能。我们进一步提供了理论分析，表明在所陈述的假设下，与穷举分裂搜索相比，DICS不会降低分类树的性能。DICS可集成到分类树、随机森林和梯度提升中。
tldr: 提出了一种基于聚类的数据知情质心分裂方法，通过类感知先验减少分裂搜索空间，在保持分类性能的同时显著提升决策树训练效率。
en_tdlr: Proposes a clustering-based Data-Informed Centroid Splitting method that reduces the split search space via class-aware priors, significantly improving decision tree training efficiency while preserving classification performance.
